title: Nilpotent lifting of an etale neighbourhood pushout
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I,J\subseteq A$ ideals with $J^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$, and $A_0=A/J$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Let $C$ be a finite type commutative $A$-algebra and $B_0$ a finite type commutative $A_0$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Put $C_0=C/JC$. Suppose $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$, $\operatorname{Spec}B_0\to\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A_0\setminus V(IA_0)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism], and $h_0:B_0\to C_0$ is an etale $A_0$-algebra map inducing an isomorphism $B_0/IB_0\xrightarrow{\sim}C_0/IC_0$. Then there exist a finite type commutative $A$-algebra $B$, an etale $A$-algebra map $h:B\to C$, and an $A_0$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:B/JB\xrightarrow{\sim}B_0$ such that the reduction of $h$ equals $h_0\circ\beta$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$.

source.place: Tag 0ALT (lemma-lift-approximation), full statement and displayed diagrams; nilpotent ideal J is in the base ring A.

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}C_0$ and $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$. Let $U=X\setminus V(I)$, and put $U_0=U\times_XX_0$, $W=Z\times_XU$, $W_0=Z_0\times_XU$ and $V_0=Y_0\times_{X_0}U_0$. The quotient base-change statement identifies $Z\times_XX_0=Z_0$. Choose $N\ge1$ with $J^N=0$. Every prime contains $J$, so $X_0\to X$ is a thickening; its base change $U_0\to U$ is again a thickening. The square $W_0\to Z_0$, $W_0\to V_0$, $Z_0\to Y_0$, $V_0\to Y_0$ is cartesian, its lower map is open, and its right map is etale by the hypothesis on $h_0$. The isomorphism $B_0/IB_0\simeq C_0/IC_0$ says that $Z_0\to Y_0$ is an isomorphism over the closed subscheme cut out by $I$, hence also over its reduced closed complement of $V_0$. Thus it is an elementary distinguished square with exactly the conditions stated in the universal-pushout lemma.

source.place: Tag 0ALT (lemma-lift-approximation), setup through the first elementary distinguished square; quotient base change as cited.

proof.text: By the hypotheses, $W\to U$ and $V_0\to U_0$ are etale. Apply thickening invariance of etale scheme objects to $U_0\hookrightarrow U$ to choose an etale scheme $V\to U$ with a specified isomorphism $V\times_UU_0\simeq V_0$. The same equivalence is fully faithful on $W,V$: the given $U_0$-map $W_0\to V_0$ lifts uniquely to a $U$-map $q:W\to V$. Since both source and target are etale over $U$, etale cancellation makes $q$ etale. Regard $V$ as an $X$-scheme through the open subscheme $U$.

source.place: Tag 0ALT, topological invariance paragraph; etale.tex Tag 039R (theorem-remarkable-equivalence), also spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 05ZS (lemma-thickening-equivalence).

proof.text: The affine-source separatedness lemma makes $Z_0\to Y_0$ separated. Since $W_0=Z_0\times_{Y_0}V_0$, separated base change makes $q_0:W_0\to V_0$ separated. The maps $W_0\hookrightarrow W$ and $V_0\hookrightarrow V$ are base changes of the thickening $U_0\hookrightarrow U$. Consequently the thickening invariance of separatedness applies to the morphism of thickenings $(q_0,q)$ and proves that $q$ is separated. No affineness of the punctured opens $W_0,V_0$ and no flatness of $Z\to X$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0ALT, separatedness sentence; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 09ZY (lemma-thicken-property-morphisms), part (6).

proof.text: Apply the open/separated-etale pushout theorem over $X$ to $W\hookrightarrow Z$ and $q:W\to V$. It gives an algebraic space $Y/X$ with $V\hookrightarrow Y$ open, $a:Z\to Y$ etale, $Z\times_YV=W$, and an isomorphism over the reduced complement. Apply the universal-pushout lemma to its base change $Y_{X_0}=Y\times_XX_0\to Y$. Its three other vertices are $Z_0,V_0,W_0$, using the specified lift isomorphism. The square with fourth vertex $Y_0$ from Step 1 is also a pushout by the same lemma. The two universal properties give mutually inverse maps $Y_{X_0}\rightleftarrows Y_0$, commuting with the maps from $Z_0$ and $V_0$: their composites restrict to the identity on both legs and so are identities by uniqueness. In particular $a$ reduces to the given map $\operatorname{Spec}h_0$ under this specified isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0ALT, pushout construction and comparison after base change; spaces-pushouts.tex Tags 0DVJ and 0DVI; spaces-perfect.tex Tag 08GN.

proof.text: Thickening base change makes $Y_{X_0}\hookrightarrow Y$ a representable closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism. Its source is the affine scheme $Y_0$ by Step 4. For every scheme test $T\to Y$ its pullback is a closed immersion of schemes, hence finite by the closed-immersion finiteness lemma. It is also surjective on point classes by the thickening assertion. Thus the finite-surjective affine-source descent lemma for algebraic spaces applies and shows that $Y$ is represented by an affine scheme. Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ over $X$.

source.place: Tag 0ALT, affineness sentence; spaces-limits.tex Tag 07VS (lemma-affine), the finite closed-immersion case of the cited Tag 07VT (proposition-affine).

proof.text: Affine contravariance gives $A\to B$ and $h:B\to C$. The quotient base-change formula and the isomorphism of Step 4 give a specified $A_0$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:B/JB\simeq B_0$. Commutation on the $Z_0$ leg says exactly $\overline h=h_0\circ\beta$. Since $a:Z\to Y$ is etale and both spaces are now schemes, $h$ is an etale algebra map. To prove finite type, choose finitely many $A_0$-algebra generators of $B_0$ and lift them via $\beta$ to $b_1,\ldots,b_r\in B$. Let $D=A[b_1,\ldots,b_r]\subseteq B$. Surjectivity modulo $JB$ gives $B=D+JB$. For every $n\ge1$, this implies $J^nB\subseteq D+J^{n+1}B$, since the coefficients in $J^n\subseteq A$ preserve $D$. Induction gives $B=D+J^nB$ for every $n$, and $J^NB=0$ gives $B=D$. This proves finite type, including an empty generator list.

source.place: Tag 0ALT, final sentence, with finite-generation lifting through the nilpotent base ideal written out.

proof.text: Finally base change the pushout of Step 4 along $Y_U=Y\times_XU\to Y$. The universal-pushout lemma says that the resulting square is a pushout. Since $Z\times_XU=W$, $W\times_XU=W$, and $V\times_XU=V$ (all maps of $W,V$ to $X$ factor through $U$), this is the pushout of $W\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}W$ and $q:W\to V$. Its fourth vertex is canonically $V$: a compatible pair of maps out of $W,V$ is uniquely its map out of $V$. Hence $Y_U\simeq V$ over $U$. The chosen map $V\to U$ is etale, proving that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over $X\setminus V(I)$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0ALT, final assertion on etaleness away from V(I), expanded by base change of the constructed square.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0ALT (lemma-lift-approximation), complete pushout proof; last sentence expanded by nilpotent generator lifting and base change to U.
